config.title: Capacitor Build Pipeline

intro.title: Capacitor Build Pipeline
intro.body: In this lesson, you will learn how to build and prepare your Ionic Angular app for native platforms using the Capacitor build pipeline. You will understand the core concept of a build pipeline, which is a sequence of automated steps that transform your web code into a native app package. The main technologies involved are the Capacitor CLI commands for syncing web assets, adding native platforms like Android or iOS, and building the final app. By the end, you'll be able to generate a native app bundle ready for testing or distribution.
intro.usecase: The Capacitor build pipeline is essential for deploying Ionic apps to app stores and production environments. This pattern appears when developers need to generate platform-specific builds (iOS .ipa or Android .apk files) for submission to Apple App Store or Google Play Store. Concrete examples include creating production builds with optimized assets for a fitness tracking app, generating release versions of a banking application with proper signing certificates, or building platform-specific versions of an e-commerce app with native device features. Every mobile app that reaches end-users goes through this build process to ensure proper packaging, code optimization, and platform compliance.

objectives: Apply the Capacitor CLI to initialize a new Capacitor project within an existing Ionic Angular application.
Implement platform-specific builds by adding iOS and Android platforms using Capacitor commands.
Utilize the capacitor.config.ts file to configure application metadata including app name and bundle identifier.
Execute build commands to generate web assets for the Ionic Angular application.
Use the Capacitor sync command to copy web assets and update native project configurations.
Access native platform projects by opening them in their respective IDEs (Xcode for iOS, Android Studio for Android).
Construct production-ready application bundles by building native projects through platform-specific tools.
Modify capacitor.config.ts settings to customize build outputs and platform-specific configurations.
Invoke the Capacitor copy command to transfer updated web assets to native project directories.
Control the build pipeline sequence by executing commands in the correct order: build → sync → open → run.
Define environment-specific configurations to manage different build settings for development and production.
Implement live reload capabilities by configuring the Capacitor development server for testing on devices.

steps.title: Import Capacitor CLI commands
steps.instruction: Add an import statement for Capacitor CLI commands from '@capacitor/cli'.
steps.hint: Use the standard ES6 import syntax to import from the package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing from a Capacitor package
import { Camera } from '@capacitor/camera';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Capacitor CLI package is imported and ready to use for build operations.
successCriteria: The code should contain a valid import statement for '@capacitor/cli'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Capacitor CLI commands. This gives you access to the CLI functions needed for build operations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs adjustment. Make sure you're importing from '@capacitor/cli' using ES6 import syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import from '@capacitor/cli' to access the CLI commands.

steps.title: Import Ionic Angular components
steps.instruction: Add an import statement for the Ionic UI components: IonButton, IonCard, IonCardContent, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, IonContent, IonHeader, IonPage, IonTitle, and IonToolbar.
steps.hint: Import these components from '@ionic/angular/standalone' using the import statement syntax.
steps.analogousExample: import { IonButton, IonContent, IonHeader, IonPage, IonTitle, IonToolbar } from '@ionic/angular/standalone';

seedCode.App.tsx:
import { Command } from '@capacitor/cli';
// Add your import statement here

steps.expectedOutcome: The Ionic UI components are imported and available for use in your component.
successCriteria: The import statement includes all specified Ionic components from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Ionic UI components needed for the build pipeline interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some Ionic components, but make sure to include all specified ones: IonButton, IonCard, IonCardContent, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle, IonContent, IonHeader, IonPage, IonTitle, and IonToolbar.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Please import all specified Ionic components from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.

steps.title: Create the BuildPipeline component
steps.instruction: Create the BuildPipelineComponent class with @Component decorator and standalone: true
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component class. Set standalone to true and provide a template.
steps.expectedOutcome: A BuildPipelineComponent class is created with @Component decorator, standalone: true, and a basic template.
successCriteria: The component should be a class named BuildPipelineComponent with @Component decorator, standalone: true property, and a template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the BuildPipelineComponent with the correct Angular component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have: 1) @Component decorator, 2) standalone: true, 3) a template property, and 4) export class BuildPipelineComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure needs adjustment. Check that you have the @Component decorator with standalone: true and a template.

steps.title: Initialize build status state
steps.instruction: Inside your BuildPipelineComponent class, add a public property called 'buildStatus' and initialize it with the string value 'Ready'.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the component class, like 'buildStatus = 'Ready';'
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a property to track the current build status, initialized to 'Ready'.
successCriteria: The BuildPipelineComponent class contains a public property named 'buildStatus' with the string value 'Ready'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the build status state. This property will track the current status of your build pipeline.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your property is named exactly 'buildStatus' and initialized with the string 'Ready' (including quotes).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required buildStatus property. Make sure to add 'buildStatus = "Ready";' inside the BuildPipelineComponent class.

steps.title: Initialize build output state
steps.instruction: Add a property named 'buildOutput' to your BuildPipelineComponent class. Initialize it as an empty array of strings.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript syntax to declare a property with type 'string[]' and assign it an empty array '[]'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BuildPipelineComponent class now has a 'buildOutput' property that can store strings from build commands.
successCriteria: The component has a property named 'buildOutput' with type 'string[]' initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a buildOutput property to store command output. This will be useful for displaying build logs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've declared 'buildOutput' as a property with type 'string[]' and initialized it as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required buildOutput property. Add a property named 'buildOutput' with type 'string[]' and initialize it to an empty array.

steps.title: Define the sync handler
steps.instruction: Inside your BuildPipelineComponent class, define an async method named syncProject that updates the buildStatus and buildOutput properties.
steps.hint: Create an async method that sets buildStatus to 'syncing' and buildOutput to an empty string initially.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a syncProject method that updates the component's state properties.
successCriteria: The method should be async, named syncProject, and update both buildStatus and buildOutput properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the syncProject handler method that updates the component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your method is async, named syncProject, and updates both buildStatus and buildOutput properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The syncProject method is not properly defined. Check that it's async, has the correct name, and updates both state properties.

steps.title: Define the build handler
steps.instruction: Define an async method named 'buildProject' inside your BuildPipelineComponent class. This method should update the 'buildStatus' and 'buildOutput' properties.
steps.hint: Add an async method that sets buildStatus to 'building', then updates buildOutput with a message, and finally sets buildStatus to 'built'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an async buildProject method that updates buildStatus and buildOutput properties.
successCriteria: The method must be named 'buildProject', be async, and update both 'buildStatus' and 'buildOutput' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the build handler method that updates the build status and output.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your method is async and updates both buildStatus and buildOutput properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't defined correctly. Check that it's async and updates both status and output properties.

steps.title: Define the copy handler
steps.instruction: Define an async method named copyWebAssets() in your BuildPipelineComponent class. This method should update buildStatus to 'copying', set buildOutput to 'Copying web assets...', simulate a delay,
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as the syncProject method: update the component properties, use a Promise with setTimeout to simulate work, then update the properties again.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a copyWebAssets() method that simulates the Capacitor copy command by updating build status and output messages.
successCriteria: The method must be named copyWebAssets, be async, return Promise<void>, update buildStatus and buildOutput properties, and include a simulated delay using Promise with setTimeout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the copy handler that simulates the Capacitor copy command workflow.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your method is async, returns Promise<void>, and updates both buildStatus and buildOutput properties correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The copyWebAssets method is missing or doesn't match the required structure. Make sure it's an async method that updates the component's state properties.

steps.instruction: update buildOutput to 'Web assets copied successfully!' and set buildStatus to 'copied'.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as the syncProject method: update the component properties, use a Promise with setTimeout to simulate work, then update the properties again.
steps.feedbackPartial: Review the instruction and try again.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Create the page structure
steps.instruction: In your BuildPipelineComponent template, return an IonPage containing an IonHeader and IonContent. The IonHeader should contain an IonToolbar with an IonTitle showing 'Build Pipeline'.
steps.hint: Use the Ionic page structure pattern: IonPage as the root, IonHeader for the top bar, and IonContent for the main content area.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of basic Ionic page structure
@Component({
  selector: 'app-example',
  standalone: true,
  template: `
    <ion-page>
      <ion-header>
        <ion-toolbar>
          <ion-title>Example Page</ion-title>
        </ion-toolbar>
      </ion-header>
      <ion-content>
        <!-- Main content goes here -->
      </ion-content>
    </ion-page>
  `
})
export class ExampleComponent {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now has a proper Ionic page structure with header and content areas ready for further content.
successCriteria: The template contains IonPage as root element, IonHeader with IonToolbar and IonTitle showing 'Build Pipeline', and IonContent element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the basic Ionic page structure. The IonPage provides the root container, IonHeader shows the title, and IonContent is ready for your build controls and output display.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the page structure isn't complete. Make sure you have: 1) IonPage as the root element, 2) IonHeader containing IonToolbar with IonTitle showing 'Build Pipeline', and 3) IonContent element for the main area.
steps.feedbackWrong: The page structure isn't implemented correctly. You need to replace the empty template with proper Ionic page markup containing IonPage, IonHeader, and IonContent elements.

steps.title: Add build status display
steps.instruction: Inside your component's template, add an IonCard element with an IonCardHeader and IonCardTitle to display the current buildStatus value.
steps.hint: Use the Ionic components to create a card that shows the build status. The buildStatus property is already available in your component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of displaying a status in a card
<IonCard>
  <IonCardHeader>
    <IonCardTitle>Status: {{ currentStatus }}</IonCardTitle>
  </IonCardHeader>
</IonCard>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will include a card that displays the current build status using Ionic components.
successCriteria: The template should contain an IonCard with IonCardHeader and IonCardTitle that displays the buildStatus property value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a card to display the current build status. This provides clear visual feedback to users about the pipeline state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct Ionic components (IonCard, IonCardHeader, IonCardTitle) and displaying the buildStatus property value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The card structure for displaying build status isn't quite right. Remember to use IonCard, IonCardHeader, and IonCardTitle components, and display the buildStatus property value within the card title.

steps.title: Add build control buttons
steps.instruction: Add three IonButton components to your template for Sync, Build, and Copy operations. Wire their (click) events to the syncProject handler and placeholder handlers for build and copy.
steps.hint: Use IonButton with the (click) event binding. For now, you can use placeholder method names for build and copy that you'll define later.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding Ionic buttons with click handlers
<IonButton (click)="syncProject()">Sync</IonButton>
<IonButton (click)="buildProject()">Build</IonButton>
<IonButton (click)="copyAssets()">Copy</IonButton>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will have three buttons for Sync, Build, and Copy operations, with the Sync button wired to the existing syncProject handler.
successCriteria: Template contains three IonButton elements with (click) event bindings to appropriate handler methods (syncProject and placeholder methods for build/copy).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the build control buttons with proper click handlers. The Sync button is connected to your existing syncProject method.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have exactly three IonButton elements with proper (click) event bindings. The Sync button should call syncProject(), and the others should have placeholder handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required three IonButton elements with click handlers. Check that you're using IonButton components with (click) event bindings.

steps.title: Add build output display
steps.instruction: In your component's template, add an IonCard with IonCardContent to display the buildOutput string.
steps.hint: Use the Ionic card components to create a structured display area for your build output text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a card element that displays the current build output text.
successCriteria: The template should contain an IonCard with IonCardContent that displays the buildOutput property using string interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added a card to display the build output. The buildOutput string will now be visible in the UI whenever it changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using IonCard and IonCardContent components with proper string interpolation to display the buildOutput property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The build output display isn't quite right. You need to add an IonCard containing IonCardContent that shows the buildOutput property value.
